before.title: 48V Integrated Starter-Generator / DC-DC Converter Failure Causing Sudden Power Loss and No-Restart
before.description: Multiple owners of facelift W213 E-Class models with the M256 mild-hybrid system reported sudden warning messages, loss of charging, reduced power, stalling, or a no-start condition traced to the 48V system. Mercedes issued service communications and there are numerous owner complaints describing failure of the integrated starter-generator or associated DC-DC converter/48V battery support hardware. When the 48V system drops offline, the vehicle may illuminate multiple warnings and can become undriveable or fail to restart.
before.solution: Scan the vehicle for 48V powertrain and charging faults, verify 12V and 48V battery state, and inspect freeze-frame data for ISG/DC-DC converter shutdown events. Dealers typically update control-unit software and replace the failed DC-DC converter, integrated starter-generator, or related 48V components as needed. Battery support and proper post-repair coding/adaptation are important to prevent repeat faults.
symptoms: Check engine light or multiple warning lights
Sudden loss of power or limp mode
Engine shuts off at a stop and will not restart

communityRecommendations.content: If buying used, check service history for prior 48V battery, ISG, or DC-DC converter replacement and ask whether the latest powertrain software campaigns were completed.
Owners recommend scanning with a Mercedes-capable tool rather than a generic OBD reader because many 48V faults are stored in submodules not visible to basic scanners.

before.title: Fuel Pump Delivery Module Failure Leading to Extended Crank, Stalling, or No-Start
before.description: A number of late-model E-Class owners reported hard starting, long crank times, hesitation, and occasional stalling traced to low-pressure fuel supply faults, including in-tank fuel pump or delivery module issues. Mercedes service literature for related models and owner reports point to intermittent fuel pressure loss rather than a high-pressure pump problem in some cases. Symptoms can be sporadic at first and become a complete no-start as the pump weakens.
before.solution: Measure low-side fuel pressure during crank and under load, compare commanded versus actual values, and inspect pump current draw and fuel pump control operation. Repair usually involves replacing the in-tank fuel pump/delivery module and sealing ring, then clearing adaptations and verifying pressure stability on a road test. If contaminated fuel is suspected, inspect the tank and filter components as well.
symptoms: Whining noise from fuel tank area

communityRecommendations.content: Owners recommend not ignoring occasional long-crank events; capturing fuel pressure data early can prevent getting stranded later.
Use top-tier fuel and avoid repeatedly running the tank very low, which forum members say may accelerate pump wear from heat.

proposal.title: Fuel Pump Delivery Module Failure Leading to Extended Crank, Stalling, or No-Start
proposal.description: Recall 23V445 and campaign 2023070012 directly cover certain 2021-2023 E-Class platform 213/238 vehicles whose fuel-pump impeller may deform, contact the housing and stop the pump. The official sequence can include warning messages, rough running and loss of propulsion. It does not establish the frozen 2024 scope, every listed engine, or a separate delivery-module electronics failure.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for campaign 2023070012. An authorized Mercedes-Benz dealer replaces the fuel-pump module under the recall where applicable. Do not buy a fuel pump or delivery module from this page; recall eligibility and the exact VIN-specific module are not established here.
symptoms: fuel delivery diagnosed when recall is not applicable

before.title: MBUX / Instrument Cluster Black Screen, Rebooting, and Rear Camera Inoperative Due to Infotainment Software Faults
before.description: Owners of 2021+ facelift E-Class cars frequently reported MBUX display freezes, black screens, spontaneous reboots, loss of audio/navigation, and backup camera malfunctions. Mercedes has issued software-related service information for MBUX and camera behavior, and NHTSA complaints describe the center display or cluster going dark while driving. In some cases the issue also disables parking aids or leaves the rearview image unavailable when reversing.
before.solution: Confirm software level of the MBUX head unit, instrument cluster, and camera control modules, then perform guided updates and fault tracing. If software does not resolve the issue, dealers may replace the display, head unit, LVDS cable, or camera module depending on stored faults and reproducibility. Low-voltage battery health should also be checked because undervoltage can trigger repeated module resets.
symptoms: No sound from media or phone

communityRecommendations.content: Before replacing hardware, owners recommend checking for pending software updates and documenting the exact conditions when the screen fails so the dealer can reproduce it.
If the issue is intermittent, record a phone video of the black screen or camera failure; forum users say this helps dealers justify module replacement under warranty.
